featured.title: NIGERIA 2027: CAN THE OPPOSITION AGREE ON A COMMON PRESIDENTIAL CANDIDATE?
featured.summary: Discussions about a possible common opposition candidate continue, but reporting describes disagreements involving the camps associated with Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. Differences over political platforms, leadership, candidate selection and party ambitions remain obstacles. A united ticket should not be assumed to have been agreed.
featured.analysis: The challenge for Nigeria's opposition is to turn discussions about unity into a credible and transparent arrangement. A successful coalition would need agreement on candidate selection, policy priorities, campaign organisation and how supporters of different parties would work together. A shared opposition position alone does not guarantee that voters will support a single candidate.
featured.editorialPerspective: RadiantWaves Media believes Nigerians should assess all parties by their policies, records, integrity and practical plans for the cost of living, employment, security and public services—not campaign promises alone.
featured.imageAlt: Image accompanying coverage of Nigeria's 2027 opposition discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi
featured.verificationStatus: Reporting attributed to the publisher; no final opposition agreement established

topStories.title: USA: Rising Household Costs Put Pressure on Republicans Ahead of Midterms
topStories.summary: Fuel and grocery costs are major concerns ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 78% of Americans surveyed blamed Trump's policies for prices rising faster than their earnings. The poll reflects public opinion and does not, by itself, establish the cause of every price increase.
topStories.verificationStatus: Source attribution supplied; verify the original report before republication

topStories.title: CANADA: Carney Rejects US Allegations of Election Interference
topStories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has rejected US allegations that Canadian politicians are interfering in American midterm elections. The dispute adds to tensions over tariffs, trade and diplomatic relations. The allegations remain contested.
topStories.verificationStatus: Source attribution supplied; verify the original report before republication

topStories.title: UK: Retail Sales Fall as Consumers Face Pressure Ahead of Christmas
topStories.summary: Retail sales volumes in Great Britain fell by 0.4% in September, according to the Office for National Statistics. The decline follows a rise in August. Weak consumer confidence and pressure on household budgets are concerns for retailers heading into the Christmas trading period.
topStories.verificationStatus: Official source supplied; confirm that the linked bulletin supports the stated figures

topStories.title: EUROPE: Paris Prepares for Further Demonstrations
topStories.summary: Paris is preparing for further demonstrations following recent unrest and damage to businesses. Authorities face the challenge of protecting the public and property while respecting the right to peaceful protest.
topStories.verificationStatus: Source attribution supplied; verify the original report before republication

topStories.title: ASIA: Taiwan Assesses Damage After Typhoon Champi
topStories.summary: Reports say Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on 24 October, leaving one person dead and 527 people injured. The storm reportedly damaged property, disrupted flights and cut electricity. Confirm casualty and damage figures against the latest official update before republication.
topStories.verificationStatus: Source attribution supplied; casualty figures require confirmation against the original report

topStories.title: AFRICA: Health Officials Investigate Possible Links Between Ebola Cases
topStories.summary: Health officials are investigating whether the first confirmed Ebola patients in Nigeria and Kenya crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe International Airport. Nigerian authorities reportedly began contact tracing after a case involving a traveller who had returned from Uganda. The investigation is ongoing; a possible connection between cases is not proof of where infection occurred.
topStories.verificationStatus: Source attribution supplied; investigation described as ongoing

topStories.title: NIGERIA: APC Opens 2027 Campaign in Kaduna
topStories.summary: Reporting says the APC is opening its 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna on 24 October. The campaign comes as voters continue to assess the administration's record on living costs, security, employment and public services. A campaign announcement is not evidence of electoral support or future results.
topStories.verificationStatus: Source attribution supplied; verify the event and report before republication

topStories.title: NIGERIA 2027: Atiku and Obi Camps Face Challenges Over a Common Ticket
topStories.summary: Opposition figures continue to discuss a possible consensus presidential candidate. Reporting describes disagreements over party platforms, candidate selection and political leadership. No common ticket should be presented as agreed unless the relevant parties formally confirm it.
topStories.verificationStatus: Reporting attributed to the publisher; no final agreement established

topStories.title: NIGERIA 2027: Kaduna Campaign Highlights the Importance of Voter Accountability
topStories.summary: The Kaduna campaign opening places attention on the North's electoral importance and on the issues that may shape voter choices. Security, food prices, employment, public services, electoral transparency and measurable delivery are relevant issues for voters to examine across parties.
topStories.verificationStatus: Source attribution supplied; analysis and political assessments should remain attributed to the publisher

topStories.title: GLOBAL ECONOMY: Oil Prices and Market Uncertainty Raise Cost Concerns
topStories.summary: Middle East tensions and concerns about energy supplies have contributed to uncertainty in oil prices and global markets. Higher energy costs can affect transport, food distribution and household bills. Market movements can change quickly, so current prices and the specific causes of movements should be checked before publication.

publicInterestFeature.title: What Should Voters Demand From Their Leaders?
publicInterestFeature.summary: As elections approach, citizens face important choices about economic results, security, integrity and the quality of public services.
publicInterestFeature.body: Campaign promises should be assessed against evidence. Voters can examine past performance, published policies, realistic funding plans and independent reporting. Accountability requires measurable commitments and honest explanations when targets are missed.
